title: Densest admissible patterns of primes n^3 + h
statement: Call a set H of positive integers admissible for n^3 + h if for every prime p there is an integer n with n^3 + h not divisible by p for all h in H; equivalently the residues -h (mod p) miss one of the values of n^3 (mod p), 0 included (all p residues when p = 3 or p = 2 mod 3, and (p+2)/3 of them when p = 1 mod 3). Only primes p <= 3|H| - 2 need checking. Let m(k) be the least m such that an admissible k-set lies in [1, m]. Determine m(k); the headline cell is k = 50: find an admissible 50-set with largest element below 255.
submission: Text file: 50 distinct positive integers h, separated by spaces or newlines.
score: the largest element of the set (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: an admissible 50-set with largest element 255 found by a randomized greedy sieve (tools/cubic_admissible.py sieve)

context: Admissible patterns govern the Hardy-Littlewood and Bateman-Horn predictions for prime constellations: for linear shifts n + h the least width H(k) is the classical table behind bounded gaps between primes, and for n^2 + h the analogous least sets are the problem quad-admissible. The cubic family is the next case and mixes two behaviours: at primes p = 2 (mod 3) cubing is a bijection, so the condition is the linear one, while at primes p = 1 (mod 3) only (p+2)/3 cube classes need to be missed, so covering them is easier and admissibility harder. The values differ from both neighbours already at k = 5 (14, against 13 for n^2 + h and 13 for shifted linear tuples).
references: P. T. Bateman, R. A. Horn, A heuristic asymptotic formula concerning the distribution of prime numbers, Math. Comp. 16 (1962) 363-367
D. H. J. Polymath, Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes, arXiv:1407.4897
W. Banks, K. Ford, Sets of integers satisfying Bateman-Horn statistics, arXiv:2605.01155

novelty.verdict: new. No table of least admissible shift sets for n^3 + h was found (arXiv), and the sequence m(k) is not in the OEIS.
closest: The linear admissible tuples H(k) and our quadratic problem quad-admissible: the same question for other polynomial families.

first_values.note: Exact values by exhaustive search (tools/cubic_admissible.py exact); the sieve reproduces m(12) = 45 and m(16) = 63 and gives the upper bounds for larger k.

baseline.text: 255 for k = 50, held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the set in `refs/cubic-admissible.txt`. Lower bound m(50) >= m(16) = 63; nothing better is proved.

bound.source: m(k) is non-decreasing and m(16) = 63 exactly
